step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify entities from the visual diagram and audio description: ALB, EC2, and ECS within the COMPUTE cluster; SageMaker (branding icon, Notebook, Model Endpoint, Model Training) within the MACHINE LEARNING cluster; DynamoDB; S3 Data Lake bucket; EMR cluster; and S3 Dataset bucket.
2. Map entities to valid AWS services: ALB ('ALB'), EC2 ('EC2'), ECS ('ECS'), DynamoDB ('DynamoDB'), EMR ('EMR'), S3 buckets ('S3'), and SageMaker components ('SageMaker').
3. Define logical flows:
   - Flow 0 (Batch Data Pipeline & ML Offline Testing): EMR reads raw data from S3 Data Lake, aggregates it into an S3 Dataset bucket, which is consumed by SageMaker Notebooks for offline model validation.
   - Flow 1 (Online Prediction Ingress & Inference): Incoming ad cross-promotion requests arrive via ALB to the ECS application layer. ECS queries DynamoDB for business rules and user features, then calls the SageMaker Model Endpoint to predict install probabilities across ad campaigns.

graph.name: Voodoo Mobile Game Cross-Promotion Machine Learning Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture handles ~100 million SageMaker model invocations and billions of predictions daily to optimize in-game cross-promotion ad serving for Voodoo mobile games.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Elastic Container Service executing business filter logic, feature collection, and endpoint invocation.

nodes.notes: NoSQL database storing business filter rules and user features required for ML model input.

nodes.name: EMR
